clue.text: What old Lib-Dem leader might assume is like junk

definitions.text: What old Lib-Dem leader might assume
definitions.meaning: read as three words: a habit (a monk's robe, something one puts on or assumes) for Ming Campbell, a former leader of Britain's Liberal Democrats
junk is slang for heroin, a drug that creates addiction

explanation.surface: A jibe that a former party leader's habits are as bad as hard drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as HABIT FOR MING: a garment Sir Menzies (Ming) Campbell, the Liberal Democrat leader of 2006-07, might put on.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard drugs such as heroin are addictive, so something like junk causes dependency.

clue.text: Chopper that's seen on helipad squashed the cat

parts.note: a helipad is marked with a large letter H

indicators.note: squashed means crushed out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A helicopter squashing a cat on the landing pad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chopper' and 'helipad' suggest a helicopter; it is an axe.
explanation.definitionFit: A small axe is a tool for chopping, so a chopper.

clue.text: Group book promotion piece

parts.note: Blur is a British pop group

explanation.surface: A band's book being promoted.
explanation.definitionFit: The short publicity text on a book jacket is a piece written to promote it.

clue.text: Hints for going round functions in drunken state

indicators.note: going round means surrounding, so the hints enclose the functions

parts.note: tips are hints
sines are trigonometric functions

explanation.surface: Advice for doing the rounds of parties while drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Being slightly drunk is a drunken state, a synonym.

clue.text: Tyro at hockey showing promise

indicators.note: showing means on display within the words, so the answer sits in the run of letters

explanation.surface: A hockey beginner who shows promise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'showing promise' reads as one phrase; 'promise' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A solemn vow is a promise.

clue.text: Test appeal in gracious good behaviour

indicators.note: in means the test and appeal go inside the exclamation

parts.note: my! and gracious! are both exclamations of surprise
an oral is a spoken test
it is sex appeal

explanation.surface: An exam on charm within polite good manners.
explanation.definitionFit: Virtuous conduct is good behaviour, a near synonym.

clue.text: Such an unfortunate situation presently available

parts.note: presently can mean at present, now
in, as a shop item that is in stock and available

explanation.surface: An unlucky predicament now on offer.
explanation.definitionFit: A situation where every option ends in loss is unfortunate, since winning is impossible.

clue.text: Mother to sing swallowing a biscuit

parts.note: ma is mother

indicators.note: swallowing means taking in, so the a goes inside the singing word

parts.note: to croon is to sing softly

explanation.surface: Mum singing while eating a cookie.
explanation.definitionFit: An almond cake made with egg white is a type of biscuit.

clue.text: Leg-puller perhaps plants 'X' on professor

indicators.note: on means placed on top of, so the number comes before the professor in this down entry

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten
a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: A joker putting a cross on a professor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leg-puller' suggests a teaser; a hamstring cord literally pulls the leg.
explanation.definitionFit: Cords of tissue join muscles to bones and pull the leg when they move, an example.

clue.text: From Yorkshire, the odd safe blower

parts.note: in Yorkshire dialect 'the' is shortened to t'
rum means odd or strange
peter is old criminal slang for a safe

explanation.surface: An eccentric Yorkshire safecracker who blows safes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'safe blower' looks like a safecracker; 'blower' alone is the definition, one who blows a brass instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A player of a brass instrument blows into it, so a blower is a musician of that kind.

clue.text: Mammal cry is audible

indicators.note: something audible is heard, so the cry's word is taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: a wail is a mournful cry

explanation.surface: An animal whose call can be heard.
explanation.definitionFit: The great sea creature is a mammal, an example of the class.

clue.text: Cooker hurt one of the little people

parts.note: a hob is the cooking surface of a cooker
bit, as in was bitten and hurt by a dog

explanation.surface: Someone burnt on the stove, injured alongside a leprechaun.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolkien's halflings are small folk, a playful example of little people.

clue.text: Boy engrossed by a Country and Western star

indicators.note: engrossed by means absorbed within, so the boy goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: a land is a country
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A boy wrapped up in a country and western singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country and Western' looks like the music genre; 'Country' gives LAND and 'Western star' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hollywood actor starred in the cowboy film Shane, so he was a star of westerns.

clue.text: Draw from favourite part of engine

parts.note: to tap a barrel is to draw liquid from it
a pet is a favourite

explanation.surface: Taking a favourite component out of an engine.
explanation.definitionFit: This lever or rod opens a valve in a car engine, so it is one component of it.

clue.text: Bears ridicule

definitions.meaning: two bears named after A. A. Milne's Winnie-the-Pooh

explanation.definitionFit: Milne's bear doubled makes the bears; the same word is a verb meaning dismiss with scorn.

clue.text: Run into second rustic only perversely awkward

indicators.note: into means the letter for run is placed inside the rest
perversely means turned the wrong way, so the dialect word is written backwards

parts.note: nobbut is a northern country dialect word for only
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Bumping into a country bumpkin who is being deliberately difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rustic only' is a single idea: the dialect word NOBBUT, which 'perversely' turns to TUBBON before R goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: An awkward, obstinate person is unwilling to be moved, a synonym.

clue.text: Building primarily engaged in H2O application

definitions.text: Building primarily engaged in H2O application

parts.words: Building primarily engaged in H2O application
parts.note: a building whose main business is applying water to people, that is, bathing them

explanation.surface: A bureaucratic description of a waterworks.
explanation.definitionFit: A public establishment for bathing is a building whose whole job is applying water to bodies.

clue.text: Imprisons criminal with financial penalties

parts.note: a con is a convict
fines are money penalties

explanation.surface: A lawbreaker is jailed and also charged money.
explanation.definitionFit: To shut someone in is to restrict them, so imprisons is a synonym.

clue.text: Apollo perhaps wanders about in fashion

parts.note: to moon about is to wander aimlessly
hot means fashionable

explanation.surface: The Greek god drifting about stylishly.
explanation.walkthrough: Apollo looks like the Greek god; here it is the American space programme.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apollo missions flew to the Moon, so one is an example of a lunar launch.

clue.text: It's involved in keeping quiet!

indicators.note: in means the rearranged letters go inside the word for silence

parts.note: mum means silent

indicators.note: involved means tangled, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A remark that this condition is all about saying nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark flags an all-in-one: the wordplay, read as a sentence, also describes refusing to speak. The apostrophe is ignored when the letters are mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Inability or refusal to speak is a condition of staying silent.

clue.text: Intoxicated, this person in grip of shakes relapsed

indicators.note: being in the grip of something means being held inside it
relapsed means fallen back, so the letters for the shakes run backwards

parts.note: DTs, delirium tremens, are the drinker's shakes
one can stand for the speaker, as in 'one does one's best'

explanation.surface: A drunk falling back into the shakes.
explanation.definitionFit: High on drink or drugs, a slang synonym for intoxicated.

clue.text: Someone with passing interest in authoress right to the end

indicators.note: to the end means one letter is shifted to the last position

parts.note: Margaret Drabble is an English novelist

explanation.surface: An author whose interest in something is only fleeting.
explanation.walkthrough: The R of DRABBLE, 'right', is moved by 'to the end'.
explanation.definitionFit: An amateur who tries things casually has only a passing interest.

clue.text: Official to reward workers

parts.note: to tip someone is to reward them with money
staff are workers

explanation.surface: An officer giving bonuses to employees.
explanation.definitionFit: A court officer who carries a metal-tipped staff, so an official.

clue.text: Person making recording fade out

explanation.definitionFit: A person who tapes is one making recordings; to dwindle gradually is to fade out.

clue.text: The woman's taken in by trainee's angelic child

her refers to the woman

explanation.surface: A woman fooled by an apprentice's sweet-faced youngster.
explanation.definitionFit: A chubby winged infant in paintings is a type of angel, so it means a sweet child.

clue.text: More than one spoke of what selective school's head does

parts.note: a head teacher runs a school
GS is the abbreviation for grammar school, a selective school in Britain

explanation.surface: A spokesperson asking what the head of a grammar school does.
explanation.walkthrough: A British grammar school selects pupils by exam. Read 'run G's': what a G's head does.
explanation.definitionFit: Ladder crosspieces or chair spindles are spokes, so the plural means more than one.

clue.text: Missile to move like a cloud

definitions.meaning: a Soviet ballistic missile of Gulf War fame
to drift fast before the wind

explanation.definitionFit: The Soviet rocket is one sense; the verb means to race along like windblown clouds.

clue.text: Bring back something for the better boat

parts.note: the football pools are something a better (one who bets) plays

explanation.surface: Restoring something to improve a vessel.

explanation.definitionFit: A single-masted sailing vessel is a type of boat.

clue.text: Do backing act make Los Angeles comeback nightly?

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the word for do is reversed

parts.note: to do someone is to con them
a turn is a variety act

indicators.note: making a comeback means returning, so the city's abbreviation is reversed

explanation.surface: A backing act's comeback in Los Angeles happening every night.
explanation.definitionFit: Done at night, as owls and bats are, a synonym for nightly.

clue.text: Annoyed actor's assistant in TV

parts.note: cross means annoyed
a dresser helps an actor into costume
